description: Extract one page's main content, cleaned and structured, so you (the calling LLM) can judge it. Use this when the user wants a judgment heuristics cannot make: content quality, distinctive versus generic positioning, whether claims are supported, which questions the page leaves unanswered, or a rewrite so AI answer engines can quote it. Use analyze_urls instead when the user wants a scored GEO audit across all categories. Also use it to classify a page before a scored analysis: the output has detected_page_type (Glippy's own guess) with detected_page_type_reason, and valid_page_types (every page_type id with a one-line description). Decide the type from the text yourself, then pass it as page_type to analyze_urls (or the domain tools); where you disagree with the detected type, your reading wins. Passing page_type here as well scores this tool's contentScores for that type. Returns compact JSON: title, meta description, H1, lead paragraph, sections (heading, word count, selfContained, answerFirst and openerDangling flags, text), the most quotable passages, statistical claims and proof points, positioning signal sentences, Glippy's heuristic content scores with their failing and warning checks, and a reviewGuide listing what to judge. Base the review on the text and treat the scores as pointers, not verdicts. The beta wording checks (brand differentiation, problem and solution, social proof, authority signals, claim evidence, source attribution, methodology, definitions, comparisons and similar) are never scored, because word lists misjudge them; you may judge them yourself from the returned sections and say what you found. Reads one public page as GlippyBot and honours robots.txt: when robots.txt disallows GlippyBot from the URL, or cannot be read, nothing is fetched and the tool says why; relay that plainly and do not retry. render_mode 'auto' or 'chrome' renders in local headless Chrome like analyze_urls, still only after robots.txt allows the URL. A bot challenge or verification page, or an almost empty client-rendered shell, is reported as an error instead of being extracted (render_mode 'auto' first retries it in Chrome); a paywalled page is extracted and flagged in pageState. When recommending fixes, never advise renaming or 301-redirecting existing, established URLs to make slugs more descriptive or to match navigation labels: Glippy does not score slug/nav alignment, and slug readability is a minor signal meant for new pages. Only recommend a redirect for URLs that are actually broken (for example a path agents keep requesting that returns 404). Long pages are trimmed to max_chars (section texts first, then the lowest-ranked passages); the limits field says what was cut.

max_chars.description: Cap on the total page text returned (title, lead, sections, passages, claims, positioning signals). Defaults to 15000. Section texts are trimmed first, then the lowest-ranked quotable passages are dropped.

max_sections.description: Maximum number of sections to return, in page order. Defaults to 30.

page_type.description: What kind of page it is, as you judged it. One of: homepage (The front page of a site or brand: what it offers and where to go next); product (One product for sale, with its price, options and details); category (A shop listing of several products, often with filters and sorting); article (A news story, blog post, guide or essay); index (A news front, blog index or hub page that lists and links to other pages); docs (Technical documentation, a reference page or a dictionary entry); faq (Questions and answers, or a help-centre article about a product or service); service (A business selling a service: trades, practices, restaurants, agencies or software); lodging (A hotel, B&B, campsite or holiday rental with rooms to book); event (One event, concert or show with its date, venue and tickets); recipe (A recipe with ingredients and steps); info (Information from a government body or a nonprofit organisation); contact (Contact details, an about page, terms, privacy or an imprint); forum (A discussion thread, or a question with answers from users). Without it (or with "auto"), checks that depend on the page type are shown but not scored. An unknown value is ignored with a note. Optional here: leave it out on a first call to get detected_page_type, or pass it to score contentScores for that type.

render_mode.description: How to fetch the page. "static" (default) is a plain GlippyBot request, "auto" falls back to local headless Chrome on a bot-block (401/403/407/429/503 or empty 2xx), "chrome" always renders via Chrome. robots.txt is checked first in every mode.

url.description: Full URL of one public page, e.g. "https://example.com/pricing". Include https:// prefix.

name: extract_page_content
